title: Typed and tested
description:
Write two functions **with type hints**, exactly as shown, so a type checker (and the tests) can read them:

```python
def slugify(title: str) -> str: ...                 # "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world"
def parse_duration(text: str) -> int: ...           # "1h30m" -> 5400 seconds
```

**slugify**: lower-case; every run of characters that are not letters or digits becomes one `-`; no `-` at either end.

**parse_duration**: a sequence of number-and-unit parts with units `h`, `m`, `s` (any case), in that order, each at most once, no spaces: `"45s"`, `"2h"`, `"1h5s"`, `"90m"`. Anything else (empty text, an unknown unit, a unit twice or out of order, a missing number, leftover characters) raises `ValueError`.
hints: For `slugify`, turn every character that is not a letter or digit into a space, then split and join with `-`, like the `slug` function in lesson 5.05: `split()` already drops runs of spaces and spaces at the ends.

For `parse_duration`, walk the text one character at a time. Collect digits in a string; when a unit comes, check that a number came before it and that the unit comes later in `"hms"` than the previous one (`"hms".find(c)` gives its place, or -1 for an unknown character), then add the number times 3600, 60 or 1. Digits left over at the end, or no unit at all, are errors.
